title: Crank
full_review:
In the noisy and endlessly unpleasant "Crank" (Lions Gate), its protagonist shares a problem with many in modern culture: a need -- in his case literal -- to be constantly stimulated, with sex and violence being the drugs of choice.

Unfolding over a single day, the visually frenetic film stars Jason Statham as Chev, a Los Angeles hit man who must keep in perpetual motion after he finds out that a rival thug (Jose Pablo Cantillo) has poisoned him with a substance designed to kill him within seconds if his heart rate drops.

In trying to stay alive long enough to find a cure -- and take his bloody revenge -- he goes on a hyper-adrenalized rampage of bloody destruction across downtown L.A. Efren Ramirez plays his gay sidekick, Kaylo, and Dwight Yoakam is a doctor who helps keep him alive.

He must also break the news to his clueless girlfriend, Eve (Amy Smart) � with whom he has sex on a crowded street to raise his pulse, to the applause of onlookers � that he's not the video game programmer she thinks he is. When she learns how he really earns a living, she finds it exciting and oddly attractive, gushing at one point, "My boyfriend kills people." And while the idea of living with a contract killer doesn't really faze her, the fact that she forgets to take her birth control pills sends her into a momentary tizzy.

A dizzying hybrid of "Speed," "D.O.A." and the "Grand Theft Auto" computer game, the film by co-writers and directors Mark Neveldine and Brian Taylor loads on the video-game-style action in an empty, mindless and unrelentingly ugly exercise.

The film contains excessive and graphic violence and gore, lewd sexual content, vulgar humor, recurring partial nudity, drug use, and pervasive rough and crude language and profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
